name: Disk Operations
description: Protects against destructive disk operations like dd to devices, \ mkfs, partition table modifications, RAID management, \ btrfs/LVM/device-mapper operations, network block devices, \ and macOS diskutil erase/partition/APFS deletion

destructive_patterns.name: dd-device
destructive_patterns.description: dd to a block device will OVERWRITE all data on that device. Extremely dangerous!

destructive_patterns.name: dd-wipe
destructive_patterns.description: dd from /dev/zero or /dev/urandom to a device will WIPE all data!

destructive_patterns.name: fdisk-edit
destructive_patterns.description: fdisk can modify partition tables and cause data loss.

destructive_patterns.name: parted-modify
destructive_patterns.description: parted can modify partition tables and cause data loss.

destructive_patterns.name: mkfs
destructive_patterns.description: mkfs formats a partition/device and ERASES all existing data.

destructive_patterns.name: mkswap
destructive_patterns.description: mkswap formats a partition as a swap area, ERASING any existing data.

destructive_patterns.name: wipefs
destructive_patterns.description: wipefs removes filesystem signatures. Use with extreme caution.

destructive_patterns.name: mount-bind-root
destructive_patterns.description: mount --bind to root directory can have system-wide effects.

destructive_patterns.name: umount-force
destructive_patterns.description: umount -f force unmounts which may cause data loss if device is in use.

destructive_patterns.name: losetup-device
destructive_patterns.description: losetup modifies loop device associations. Verify before proceeding.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-stop
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --stop shuts down a RAID array. Data may become inaccessible.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-remove
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --remove removes a drive from a RAID array. May cause data loss if redundancy is lost.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-fail
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --fail marks a device as failed. Use only for intentional drive replacement.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-zero-superblock
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --zero-superblock PERMANENTLY erases RAID metadata. Array cannot be reassembled.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-create
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --create initializes a new RAID array, ERASING existing data on member devices.

destructive_patterns.name: mdadm-grow
destructive_patterns.description: mdadm --grow reshapes a RAID array. Interruption can cause data loss. Backup first.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-subvolume-delete
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs subvolume delete PERMANENTLY removes a subvolume and all its data.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-device-remove
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs device remove redistributes data off a device. Interruption causes data loss.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-device-add
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs device add incorporates a device into the filesystem. Verify the device is correct.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-balance
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs balance redistributes data across devices. Can be slow and disruptive.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-check-repair
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs check --repair is DANGEROUS and can cause data loss. Backup first!

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-rescue
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs rescue operations modify filesystem metadata. Use only as last resort.

destructive_patterns.name: btrfs-filesystem-resize
destructive_patterns.description: btrfs filesystem resize can shrink a filesystem. Data loss if size is too small.

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-remove
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup remove detaches a device-mapper device. May cause data loss if in use.

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-remove-all
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup remove_all removes ALL device-mapper devices. Extremely dangerous!

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-wipe-table
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup wipe_table replaces the device table, causing all I/O to fail.

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-clear
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup clear removes the mapping table from a device.

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-load
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup load changes device mapping. Verify the new table is correct.

destructive_patterns.name: dmsetup-create
destructive_patterns.description: dmsetup create sets up a new device-mapper device. Verify parameters carefully.

destructive_patterns.name: nbd-client-disconnect
destructive_patterns.description: nbd-client -d disconnects a network block device. Data loss if not properly unmounted.

destructive_patterns.name: nbd-client-connect
destructive_patterns.description: nbd-client connecting a device can expose or overwrite data. Verify server and device.

destructive_patterns.name: pvremove
destructive_patterns.description: pvremove ERASES LVM metadata from a physical volume. Data becomes inaccessible.

destructive_patterns.name: vgremove
destructive_patterns.description: vgremove DELETES a volume group and all logical volumes within it.

destructive_patterns.name: lvremove
destructive_patterns.description: lvremove PERMANENTLY deletes a logical volume and ALL its data.

destructive_patterns.name: vgreduce
destructive_patterns.description: vgreduce removes a physical volume from a volume group. Data may be lost.

destructive_patterns.name: lvreduce
destructive_patterns.description: lvreduce SHRINKS a logical volume. Data loss if filesystem isn't resized first!

destructive_patterns.name: lvresize-shrink
destructive_patterns.description: lvresize with negative size SHRINKS the volume. Resize filesystem first or lose data!

destructive_patterns.name: pvmove
destructive_patterns.description: pvmove migrates data between physical volumes. Do NOT interrupt or data may be lost.

destructive_patterns.name: lvconvert-merge
destructive_patterns.description: lvconvert --merge reverts LV to snapshot state, discarding changes since snapshot.

destructive_patterns.name: diskutil-erase
destructive_patterns.description: diskutil erase operations DESTROY all data on the target disk or volume.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
diskutil eraseDisk/eraseVolume/reformat/zeroDisk/randomDisk/secureErase \ overwrite the target's contents. On APFS this removes every volume in \ the container. There is no recovery without backups.

\ Inspect the target first: \ diskutil list \ diskutil info <disk>

destructive_patterns.name: diskutil-partition
destructive_patterns.description: diskutil partitioning operations rewrite the partition map and erase data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
diskutil partitionDisk erases the entire disk before writing the new \ partition map; splitPartition and mergePartitions destroy the contents \ of the partitions they reshape (merge preserves only the first when \ asked); resetFusion wipes both constituent devices.

\ Preview the current layout first: \ diskutil list <disk>

destructive_patterns.name: diskutil-apfs-delete
destructive_patterns.description: diskutil apfs delete/erase operations permanently remove APFS containers, volumes, or snapshots.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an APFS container destroys every volume inside it; deleting or \ erasing a volume destroys that volume's data; deleting a snapshot \ removes a restore point. None of these are recoverable without \ backups.

\ List APFS structure first: \ diskutil apfs list
